title: Remote engineering: close the three open review findings on 71c4ed6a
requested_outcome: The remote engineering loop was activated by owner decision at 71c4ed6af13d37d8c9d16179a553201c1e2de695 with three material findings from its exact-SHA review still open. Repair all three. (1) A requester-chosen request_id that is schema-valid but credential-shaped is copied into claims, receipts, objective/task ids, refusals, host output, source locators and the public projection. Keep request_id as the Director's identifier (the spec's Outbound visibility section promises it) but constrain it in the request schema to ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}(-[a-z0-9]{1,16}){1,7}$ and require target_branch to equal clive/objective/<request_id> exactly; refuse both without echoing the rejected value. (2) The claim is not crash-durable on first use: when the remote_engineering and claims directories are newly created, fsync each parent after introducing the directory entry, before any lifecycle write; keep file and containing-directory fsync for each claim. (3) Claim creation is check-then-write: make it an atomic O_CREAT|O_EXCL create; a loser reloads the winning claim, continues only for the same digest using its claimed_at, and refuses a different digest before lifecycle intake; apply equivalent no-clobber semantics to receipts. Test inputs whose ids do not fit the new rule may be renamed; no existing assertion may change.
acceptance_criteria: a credential-shaped request_id and a target_branch other than clive/objective/<request_id> are each refused, and the rejected value appears in no refusal, outcome, receipt, claim, host output or projection
first-ever intake is crash-durable: a fault injected after the claim is written and before the first lifecycle write leaves a claim that survives, with the new directories' parents fsynced
two overlapping controllers cannot both claim one request id: exactly one claim wins, the loser proceeds only for the same digest and refuses a different digest before any lifecycle write
every existing test in tests/test_remote_engineering.py still passes with unchanged assertions
full repository acceptance for the candidate SHA reports mechanical_evidence complete with no unsatisfied gate
